title: The migration header says a page reading the ledger during the hold phase 'waits, then proceeds', but the previous image's REPEATABLE READ pages then read ledger_match as empty
evidence: Lines 50-52, rewritten in 99579d0c: "Once held, to the end of this migration (adding seq rewrites ledger_match, ...), a reconcile, a person's ledger action or a page reading the ledger waits, then proceeds". Line 120, ADD COLUMN seq ... GENERATED ALWAYS AS IDENTITY, rewrites ledger_match, and a rewrite is not MVCC-safe. The previous image's reconciliation page runs at REPEATABLE READ: apps/web/src/lib/routes/reconciliation.ts:85 sets oneSnapshot: true, packages/db/src/authz/scope.ts:276 opens 'BEGIN ISOLATION LEVEL REPEATABLE READ', and apps/web/src/lib/reconciliation/queries.ts:478 refuses any other level; the same at cc3dd7f6. That snapshot is taken at the scope's first statement, before any ledger read. If the loop takes its locks in that gap, the page waits on its first ledger read, the migration commits, and the page then reads the new ledger_match file with the old snapshot. Every row there carries the migration's xid, so the page sees none. ledger_entry is not rewritten (only CHECKs and a trigger), so the page shows entries with no matches, and line 311's interest takes_back is lost. Probe on PG 18 with the same ALTER on a 5-row scratch table and a reader blocked on the ACCESS EXCLUSIVE lock: REPEATABLE READ saw 0 of 5 rows, READ COMMITTED saw 5. The reconcile and ledger actions run at READ COMMITTED and are unaffected. The impact is one wrong, read-only page view in a sub-second window, before launch.
fix: Make lines 50-52 accurate, and match the wording in ADR 0084 D16: a page reading at REPEATABLE READ whose snapshot began before the locks were taken reads ledger_match as empty once and reads it whole on reload. Alternatively, avoid the rewrite: add seq as a plain nullable column, fill it with an MVCC-safe UPDATE, then add the identity. That changes the migration, through the marker route.

verdict.reason:
I could not refute it. I reproduced the finding on PG 18.4, and the defect is in this PR's own change. It is a nit: the migration header is wrong about what the old app's pages see during the migration's lock.

1. Setup. I worked in my own clone at d2fdd106 and installed with --frozen-lockfile under the lock. Migration 20261110090000 is not on the base (cc3dd7f6, the merge-base with claude/build-platform). This PR added header lines 50-52 (99579d0c) and the ADD COLUMN seq GENERATED ALWAYS AS IDENTITY at line 120 (b5949dc1). That ADD COLUMN rewrites ledger_match.

2. Previous image's read path, checked at cc3dd7f6:
- apps/web/src/lib/routes/reconciliation.ts:85 sets oneSnapshot: true.
- packages/db/src/authz/scope.ts:276 opens with BEGIN ISOLATION LEVEL REPEATABLE READ.
- The first statement is SET_ACTOR, a SELECT set_config. That fixes the snapshot before any ledger table is touched or locked.
- apps/web/src/lib/reconciliation/queries.ts:478 refuses any other level.
- reconciliation() then reads ledger_match and ledger_entry, starting at queries.ts:456-460.
So the migration's NOWAIT loop can take both locks after the page's snapshot exists.

3. Probe 1, scratch tables. The same NOWAIT locks plus the ADD COLUMN identity, with a reader blocked on the lock. A REPEATABLE READ reader saw ledger_match 0 of 5 and ledger_entry 5 of 5. A READ COMMITTED reader saw 5 and 5.

4. Probe 2, the real migration file:
- I migrated a scratch database to 20261109090000 and inserted 5 synthetic ledger_match rows.
- A page session logged in as tp_app_dev followed the previous image's scope order: BEGIN, set_config actor, set_config practice_ids.
- I applied the actual 20261110090000 file as tp_owner (BEGIN, SET LOCAL ROLE, the file) and waited until it held the ACCESS EXCLUSIVE lock.
- The page's ledger_match read then waited on that lock, and I committed the migration.
Results:
- REPEATABLE READ: the read returned 0 of 5, and again 0 in the same transaction. A new transaction (a reload) read 5.
- READ COMMITTED: 5.
- tp_owner saw all 5 rows, each with a seq value.
ledger_entry is not rewritten (only CHECKs and a trigger), so the page would show entries with no matches.

5. Documentation. The header says a page 'waits, then proceeds' and calls the migration 'Safe with the previous image running'. It leaves out the empty read. Neither ADR 0084 D16 nor the design mentions it, and the first-round findings never raised it.

Two small slips in the evidence don't change the conclusion:
- 'line 311's takes_back' is current-image code (HEAD queries.ts:311), which does not run during the window. What the previous image actually loses is every match on the page: claim, posting, deposit, recoupment and interest.
- ADR 0084 D16 does not contain the wording the fix tells the header to match.

Impact: one wrong, read-only page view, correct on reload, in a sub-second window, before launch.

title: INT-REL-2 left holdings unindexed: heldInterest() is rebuilt over every interest entry and match, twice, for every take-back PLB L6 in the practice's history on every pass, though ADR 0084 and the PR say holdings come from lookups built once a pass
evidence: providerAdjustments walks every PLB L6 of the moment on every pass (remittances.ts:883, 922). recordInterest computes holdings whenever any draw is negative (remittances.ts:1038) and does so before interestWrites decides anything. That includes a historical take-back with nothing left to write. heldInterest (remittances.ts:1122-1128) spreads every entry, builds a map of every match, and runs @tp/ledger interestHeld twice over all of them. The cost per pass is (take-back L6s in history) x (interest entries), which grows quadratically with history. Micro-benchmark of the same code (tsx, @tp/ledger interestHeld): 1.4 ms per take-back L6 at 2,000 entries and matches, 26 ms at 20,000, 178 ms at 100,000. 1,000 historical take-backs at 100,000 entries cost about 178 s per pass, above the 150 s budget. At CAS-42.3's 2,000 lines it is negligible (about 1.4 s for 1,000 take-backs). CAS-42.3 (5074ce3e) measures only unnamed paying L6s. ADR 0084:259-260 ('each line's holdings through lookups built once a pass and kept current as it writes') and PR body line 103 say the opposite of what the code does for holdings.
fix: Build the holdings, per chain and per line as a whole, once in interestState and update them in recordInterest as it writes, as latestOf already is. Or at least skip an L6 whose per-sign room is already spent before computing holdings. Correct ADR 0084:259-260 and PR body line 103 if the code stays as it is. Add a take-back-heavy shape to the size test.

verdict.reason:
The finding holds, as a nit. I checked it in my own clone at d2fdd1060c9b23e7e5bf5d2560db99f8a7826d46 (removed afterwards). Verdict file: /tmp/claude-0/-home-user-PhysicalTherapy/6af08ef9-734c-5d6d-a787-51ade7156d78/scratchpad/progress/i126c-sk-money-F-M2-2.md.

What the code does (verified):
- The adjustment query in apps/worker/src/reconcile/interest-chains.ts reads every PLB L6 of nonzero amount on every loaded remittance. providerAdjustments then hands each one to recordInterest on every pass (remittances.ts:883 and 922).
- attributeInterest only computes, so a historical take-back L6 gives the same negative draws on every pass.
- recordInterest:1038 calls heldInterest(interest) whenever any draw is negative. It does this before interestWrites runs and has no early exit when nothing is left to write.
- heldInterest (remittances.ts:1122-1128) copies every interest entry, builds a new map of every interest match, and runs @tp/ledger interestHeld twice over all of them. Each take-back draw then also filters every holding.

Benchmark rerun: I ran the same heldInterest body with tsx against @tp/ledger interestHeld. It took 1.07 ms per take-back L6 at 2,000 entries, 17.8 ms at 20,000 and 149.8 ms at 100,000. The finding reported 1.4, 26 and 178 ms, so the scaling reproduces.

CAS-42.3 has no take-back case: reconcile.large.db.test.ts:180 has only paying `L6*-` rows that name no claim.

The docs overstate the fix. ADR 0084:258-260 and PR body line 103 both say "each line's holdings through lookups built once a pass and kept current as it writes". InterestState's own list of lookups has no holdings entry, and the f7e2c5de commit body admits holdings are still rebuilt, only now just for a PLB L6 that takes interest back. The PR's own ADR and PR text misdescribe its own code, and anyone can confirm that by reading it.

Where the finding overstates:
- The cost does not matter at any size the reconcile reaches today. ADR 0083:837-847 already lists reconcile time at size as a known gap handed to SUITE-CAP-3: 2,084 lines took 333 s at 0.5 vCPU, from older code. Comparing 100,000 entries with 1,000 take-backs against the 150 s budget of a 2,000-line pass is not a fair test.
- It is not a regression. On the base (cc3dd7f6), every L6 ran namedLines, which checks every case line against every match on every pass. The PR cuts that to entries plus matches, and only for take-back L6s.
- No amount is wrong.

Real, nit only. The minimum fix is to correct ADR 0084:259-260 and PR body line 103. Better: keep per-chain and per-line holdings in InterestState and update them as recordInterest writes, as latestOf already is, or skip an L6 that has nothing left to take back before computing holdings. Add a size test with many take-backs.

title: LED-R1's widening changes the case that was already right: a PLB L6 that names the correction now also credits a line the correction does not carry, so named and unnamed payment of the same interest land on different lines
evidence: interest-chains.ts:194 (84534029, moved by f7e2c5de) sets namedClaimIds to every claim of the named chain that the attribution reads (byChain.get(namedChain)). Since 84534029, that includes every claim a claim match names. attributeInterest passes this set as the draw's claimIds in steps 1, 2 and 4 (packages/ledger/src/interest.ts:254, 258, 293). recordInterest then takes paid lines from any standing claim match to any of those claims (remittances.ts:1043). A later correction never reverses an earlier claim match. recoupReversals skips a reversal that has its correction beside it in the same remittance. Proven with a database test in my clone. Setup: LED-23 original.835 (O: L1, L2), then paired.835 (R + C1 on both lines, approved), then a scratch zz-drop.835 (R2 reversing C1, plus C2 carrying L1 only, plus PLB L6 'L6:SYNCCNLED230003' paying 3.00), with a reconcile after each load. At d2fdd106 the L6's 3.00 is written as 133 on L1 and 167 on L2, allocated, and both matches name C1. With the pre-fix line (reached claims only) it writes 300 on L1, and the match names C2. With the same 3.00 paid by an unnamed L6 and C2 reporting AMT I 3.00 (step 3 pool), the head writes 300 on L1. So the PLB L6 names C2, but interest lands on L2: a line C2 does not carry, whose C1 payment the payer reversed. The granted design D5 (designs/ledger-interest-once.md:397-398, 'the claims the L6 names, in steps 1, 2 and 4') and PRD 13's granted text ('against the case lines of the claims it is for (the claims the PLB L6 names ...)', design 9.2) say otherwise. So does the PR body line 72 ('credits the lines its correction approved, as naming the correction or nothing does'). ADR 0084:116 was rewritten to the widened rule. No test covers this: named-original.835 and paired.835 keep both claims on the same lines. The per-line split is what later take-backs and line floors read. Outputs are in scratchpad/progress/i126c-money-2-head.out and i126c-money-2-base.out; the test and fixture are saved as i126c-money-2-zz-money2.db.test.ts.txt and i126c-money-2-zz-drop.835.txt.
fix: Narrow the widening to what LED-R1 needs: the claims the reference reaches plus the claims that correct them (walk forward from the reached claims to their reversals' corrections), not the chain's earlier claims. Naming the original then still reaches its correction's lines, and naming C2 reaches only C2's lines, which matches the pool. Add this shape (a second correction that drops a line, then a PLB L6 naming it) as a red database test, an LED-23 fixture and expected.json row. Correct ADR 0084 D5 (:116) and PR body line 72 to match.

verdict.reason:
I could not refute F-M2-1. It reproduces at d2fdd1060c9b23e7e5bf5d2560db99f8a7826d46, and commit 84534029 in this PR's own fix round introduced it.

How I tested: in my own clone, a scratch database test loads LED-23 original.835, then paired.835, then one third remittance, with a reconcile after each load. Every third remittance has the same shape: R2 reverses C1, C2 carries L1 only, plus one PLB L6 of 3.00. Each variant ran twice: once at the head and once with line 194 of interest-chains.ts put back to the pre-84534029 `reached` set.

| Variant | Head | Pre-84534029 line |
|---|---|---|
| A: PLB L6 names C2 (the reviewer's zz-drop.835) | L1 133, L2 167 | L1 300 |
| B: unnamed L6, C2 reports AMT I 3.00 | L1 300 | L1 300 |
| C: same as B, but the L6 names C2 | L1 133, L2 167 | L1 300 |
| D: L6 names C1 | L1 133, L2 167 | L1 133, L2 167 |
| E: L6 names the original | L1 133, L2 167 | nothing (the LED-R1 bug) |

Variant C is the cleanest proof. B and C report the same AMT I and differ only in the PLB reference. Yet the head writes 167 of the interest on L2 when the payer names C2 and none when it names nothing. L2 is a line C2 does not carry, and the payer reversed its C1 payment. Before the widening, A, B and C agreed on L1 300.

Every cited line holds at the head:
- interest-chains.ts:194 sets the claims a named draw is for to every claim of the chain that was read, through `byChain`.
- packages/ledger/src/interest.ts:254, 258 and 293 pass that set into steps 1, 2 and 4.
- remittances.ts:1043 turns those claims into paid lines from their standing claim matches.
- C1's claim match on L2 stays standing (`rev=false`).
- ADR 0084 lines 115-116 state the widened rule.
- The design's D5 at lines 397-398 and PRD 13's granted text both say the claims the PLB L6 names.
- The live PR body (head d2fdd106) still says the L6 credits "the lines its correction approved, as naming the correction or nothing does". Variant C shows that is false at the head.

No LED-23, LED-24 or LED-25 fixture has a correction carrying fewer lines than its reversal, so no existing test covers this shape.

I weighed four counter-arguments; none holds:
- **The stale C1 match on L2 is frozen principal behaviour.** True: the reconcile skips a reversal when its correction is in the same remittance. But it is the PR's widening that makes an L6 naming C2 read that match; the line before it did not.
- **The code matches ADR 0084.** It does, but this PR rewrote that ADR. The code still contradicts the granted wording and the PR's own stated rule.
- **The 3.00 is still credited once.** True, and here both lines sit in one case. But the split on each line is wrong, and later take-backs and the line floors read that split.
- **Section 10.1.** The fix only touches interest, so it is within the freeze exception.

Severity should-fix stands.

Evidence is in /tmp/claude-0/-home-user-PhysicalTherapy/6af08ef9-734c-5d6d-a787-51ade7156d78/scratchpad/progress/:

verdict.reason:

title: ADR 0084's 'At size' bullet says each line's holdings are read through lookups built once a pass, but the code rebuilds them for every take-back PLB L6
evidence:
ADR 0084:259-260 (77653d10): 'reads each claim's standing claim matches, each PLB L6's entries and each line's holdings through lookups built once a pass'. In the code, remittances.ts:1038 calls heldInterest(interest) for each PLB L6 that takes interest back. heldInterest (remittances.ts:1122-1128) copies every interest entry and runs interestHeld over every entry twice, the second time against a fresh map of every interest match. That is O(entries + matches) per take-back PLB L6, quadratic over a pass.

Micro-benchmark of that exact construction: 2.27 ms per take-back PLB L6 at 2,000 entries and matches, 12.45 ms at 10,000, 101 ms at 50,000. If every 20-claim check took interest back, that adds 0.2 s at CAS-42.3's 2,000 lines (no risk to the 150 s budget), 6.2 s at 10,000 lines and 253 s at 50,000. CAS-42.3 seeds no take-back, so this path is unmeasured, and the ADR overstates what f7e2c5de did. The commit message itself says correctly that holdings are read only for a PLB L6 that takes interest back.
fix: Correct the ADR sentence to say holdings are rebuilt for each take-back PLB L6. Or keep the per-line, per-chain holdings and the line totals current in InterestState, as latestOf is kept, and add a take-back PLB L6 to some of CAS-42.3's checks so the take-back path is measured.

verdict.reason:
I could not refute it. DB2-4 holds as a nit: a wrong sentence in this PR's own ADR, which I reproduced at d2fdd1060c9b23e7e5bf5d2560db99f8a7826d46.

1) The text matches the quote. ADR 0084 lines 259-260, added by 77653d10, a commit on this branch after merge-base cc3dd7f6, say the interest path reads "each line's holdings through lookups built once a pass and kept current as it writes."

2) The code does something else. At apps/worker/src/reconcile/remittances.ts:1038, recordInterest calls heldInterest(interest) for every PLB L6 with a negative draw. heldInterest (lines 1122-1128) copies every interest entry, runs @tp/ledger interestHeld (packages/ledger/src/interest.ts:403) over all of them, then runs it again against a new map of every interest match. That costs O(entries + matches) for each take-back PLB L6. Every pass walks every PLB L6 in the history, so the total grows quadratically when take-backs grow with history.

3) I tried to read "each line's holdings" as latestOf, which is built once a pass. remittances.ts:957 does call latestOf's key "a line's holding of a chain". That reading fails for three reasons:
- In the ADR's own words a holding is an amount held (line 118: "a holding below zero counts as zero").
- latestOf holds only each line's latest match, not the amount held.
- The code comment at line 1037 and the body of commit f7e2c5de both say the holdings are read only for a PLB L6 that takes interest back.
The ADR's other claim ("never every case line against every match for each draw") is true, but it does not make the holdings claim true.

4) The finding says CAS-42.3 seeds no take-back, and it doesn't. I checked by reading apps/worker/src/reconcile/reconcile.large.db.test.ts:167-180: it seeds only PLB L6 payments (L6*-X, entries of +50), so the take-back path is never measured. I did not run that test, because it seeds no take-back and its result would not bear on this claim.

5) I re-ran the benchmark using the real interestHeld and an exact copy of heldInterest. I got 1.35 ms per take-back PLB L6 at 2,000 entries, 9.65 ms at 10,000 and 87.6 ms at 50,000. If every check took interest back, a pass would add 0.1 s, 4.8 s and 219 s. The finding reported 2.27, 12.45 and 101 ms, the same order. At CAS-42.3's size there is no risk to the 150 s budget, so this is a nit. The ADR statement is still wrong, and the path is still unmeasured.
